purpose.intro: Config-driven identity module: registration, authentication, and account recovery described by a declarative auth DSL, executed over Ory Kratos. The module holds no flow table and no session table. Credential conversations are the provider's own flows, relayed; the session is the provider's token, carried in an HttpOnly cookie. What the module owns is the part the provider has no concept of: the product's rules (the DSL), the app's user row, consent and profile records, organizations and memberships — and the GATE, which re-checks on every request that a caller still carries what the config demands.

claims.text: **Stage 1** — auth core: the DSL engine, Kratos infra + adapter, models/repositories/services, HTTP surface + mount, web-main cutover.

**Stage 2 (this stage)** — organizations, memberships, invitations, and the gate going live on the module's own membership facts (active organization, signed-in invitation accept). See organizations.md (`./organizations.md`).

**Stage 3 (landed)** — access control (`@prowd/gated-scoped-ac`: who may perform each org action — verdicts on writes, engine-resolved row scopes on reads; role-value escalation stays a service business rule until the DSL can compare roles).

reference.statement: Two layers: the DSL can *express* a policy; the runtime must *do* it. This is what's actually wired.

reference.topic: How the app runs this module
reference.statement: The host app mounts per `api/mount-types.ts` (see `apps/api/src/mounts.ts`): authMount at its basePath (`/api/auth`), session + gate middlewares on the client surface (`/api/client`). The provider's courier SMS callback rides the module's own auth surface (`/api/auth/courier/sms`, secret-guarded, registered before the session middleware) — the app never mounts or names it, and the module-shipped `kratos.yml` is the only place that knows the URL. The module's tables enter the app's migration chain by re-export — `apps/api/src/models/index.ts` re-exports `./models`, and the app's drizzle config generates migrations from there. Table names are plain domain names, no prefix (`user`, `organization`, `member`, …; `user` is a Postgres reserved word, quoted by drizzle everywhere). Rate limiters attach on `authMount.rateLimitPaths` when the app grows them.
